summary: pixel-map-testmetest ships obfuscated install-time dropper via binding.gyp command expansion
details: The package executes an obfuscated payload on install and on require. binding.gyp declares a native target with no C/C++ source files and uses GYP command expansion (`<!(env node index.js...; echo stub.c)`) in `sources`, causing node-gyp's automatic configure step during `npm install` to shell out to index.js. index.js is a multi-layer loader: a String.fromCharCode char-code array is passed through a ROT-10 letter transform and handed to eval(); the decoded body uses node:crypto to AES-128-GCM decrypt a 318KB shipped blob (data.bin) with hardcoded key/IV/aad and executes the result. The same loader is also the package's main entry, so `require()` triggers the same decrypt-and-execute path. package.json self-describes the package as a `stub` placeholder (`"stub": true`, description: `Temporary package placeholder for staged publishing`) yet declares `bun ^1.2.18` as its sole runtime dependency, pulling in an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time. No legitimate functionality is shipped in the clear; the actual payload bytes are opaque until runtime decryption.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
